Your trade

Website for tradespeople: your work on show, quote requests straight to you

Your future customers type your trade and their town into their phone, then call the one they trust. I build the website that gets you found and shows your work, then I take care of everything.

Get found in your area

Your trade and the towns where you work are written in black and white, where Google and your customers look for them.

Show your work

Before and after photos of your jobs show the quality of your finish better than any words.

One tap to call

On a phone, a button dials your number, and a quote form gathers the details of the job.

Build trust

Insurance, qualifications, years in the trade: the customer knows who they are letting in.

What your customer wants to know in thirty seconds

Someone looking for a tradesperson nearly always has a real project or problem: a leak, a circuit breaker that keeps tripping, a front wall to repaint, a garden to rethink. They compare two or three names on their phone, sometimes from the sofa, sometimes standing in water. Your website needs to answer them quickly:

  • What you do, in the words they use: repairs, renovation, fitting, servicing.
  • Where you work: your town and the ones nearby, written out in full.
  • What your work looks like: a few photos of real jobs.
  • How to reach you: a number they can call with one tap and an online quote request.

The rest comes later. A tradesperson’s website does not need to be long. It needs to be clear, and up to date.

Reassure them before the first call

Letting someone into your home takes trust. Your website can clear up doubts before the phone even rings. Show your face and your name, your years in the trade, your qualifications (RGE, for example, if you have it) and your ten-year liability insurance if your trade requires it.

For repair call-outs, show your hourly rate and your travel costs. The customer knows what to expect, and the rules require you to state them before starting work anyway.

Photos of your jobs are still your best selling point. Get into the habit of taking before and after shots, even on your phone. Three real photos of a refitted bathroom say more than a catalogue picture.

Only publish genuine reviews. If your customers are happy, invite them to say so on your Google Business Profile, and the website links to those reviews.

One page or a showcase website?

If you do a single trade, one well-built page is enough to get started. If you offer several services, for example plumbing, heating and turnkey bathrooms, the showcase website gives each one its own page. Someone searching for “heat pump installation” then lands on the page about it, not on a catch-all text. The one page or showcase website guide helps you decide.

To be found near you, the website teams up with your Google Business Profile. The profile puts you on the map, and the website wins people over. Both must show exactly the same contact details.

You are out on the job, I take care of the website

You have neither the time nor the wish to manage a website in the evening, and that is normal. I write the text with you after a short chat, prepare the layout and put everything online. Later on, a price changes or a new photo comes in? You send it to me from your phone, and it is done.

To move fast without cutting corners, I programmed a little band of monsters that takes care of everything that repeats from one website to the next. I keep the design for myself, followed by a read-through of every page before it goes online. That is what keeps lead times short and the price low.

How much does it cost

A showcase website from a freelancer usually costs between €1,500 and €3,000. Mine is 4 to 5 times cheaper, with nothing essential taken away: I save time on the technical side, never on checking.

The build starts at €500, and that price covers up to 10 pages. You pay 25% when you order, then the rest when the site goes live, all at once or in 6 or 12 interest-free payments. The basic subscription follows, at €10 a month with no commitment: domain name, hosting, updates, backups, support, and a change by me once a quarter. Everything is detailed on the prices page.

What I recommend

Your questions

How much does a website for a tradesperson cost?

The build starts at €500, whether your site has a single page or 10. After that, the basic subscription at €10 a month covers the web address, hosting and upkeep. You know the total before you order.

I cover a large area. How can I be found everywhere?

Name the main towns and villages where you work, without listing dozens of them. An honest list on the website, and a well-set service area on your Google Business Profile, work better than one page per village.

I have hardly any photos of my jobs. Is that a problem?

No. We start with what you have, even two snaps taken on your phone. The website then grows job after job: you send me the photos, and I add them.

I already have an old website. Do I have to start again from scratch?

Nothing is lost. With the Moving your old website option, I bring over your text, your photos and your page addresses, so you keep the place you already have on Google.
